newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia court dismisses ruling against Ekran.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia court dismisses ruling against Ekran.

text.p: Malaysia's Appeals Court on Monday dismissed a High Court environmental ruling against Ekran Bhd, developer of a 13.6 billion ringgit ($5.5 billion) hydroelectric dam project.
Legal sources said the ruling will effectively allow Ekran to go ahead with development of the dam.

The court's Justice Gopal Sri Ram, who headed a three-member bench, said the Environmental Quality Act referred to by the High Court in its ruling, was not applicable in the case because that law was part of the federal constitution while the dam itself was located in the eastern state of Sarawak.
He said the earlier ruling by the High Court "is dismissed".
"The misconception here is that everybody thought the environmental act was applicable to the whole country, which is not the case when it involved a state," Justice Gopal said.
The Malaysian High Court said last June the Bakun dam project was in violation of the Environmental Quality Act because its environmental impact report was flawed.
The High Court ruled that the federal government was wrong to delegate the power to approve the environmental impact assessment to the Sarawak state government, a major shareholder in the dam.
The ruling was based on a lawsuit filed by three Sarawak tribals who opposed the construction of the dam.
G.S. Nijar, counsel for the plaintiffs, said they would appeal against Monday's ruling. ($1 = 2.49 ringgit)
